newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sets terms on gas pipelines with Russia.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sets terms on gas pipelines with Russia.

text.p: Bulgaria on Friday set out the terms it is seeking with Russia in an intergovernmental agreement on new gas pipelines to carry Russian natural gas through its territory.

Bulgaria insists on building the new pipelines and be their sole owner, Bulgargas executive director Vasil Filipov said after talks with a delegation of a Bulgarian-Russian joint stock company Topenergy, including representatives of Russia's Gazexport.

"We started talks today and we got the impression that the visiting group is not ready with acceptable for the two sides decisions being an alternative scheme after Bulgaria cancelled the two pipeline concessions for transiting Russian gas," Filipov said.
Bulgarian and Russian experts are expected to prepare by Wednesday the contracts for supplying and transiting Russian gas and building the new pipelines.
Senior Gazprom officials, headed by vice-president Bogdan Bodzulyak, will arrive in Sofia on Monday to join the negotiations.

Topenergy was set up last year by Gazprom GAZP.RTS, which has a 50 percent share, and Bulgargas, which holds a 25.1 percent stake. The remaining 24.9 percent is distributed among Bulgarian banks and firms.
"Topenergy can only invest in the construction of the new pipelines," Filipov said.
He said Bulgaria's private firm Overgas, which is half-owned by Gazprom, will supply Russian gas to Bulgarian consumers and Topenergy will ensure the transiting gas.
Bulgaria has a gas network of some 2,000 km.

An enlargement of the network will be needed because gas supplies to Turkey will be increased and the project envisages gas supplies to Greece, Macedonia, Serbia and possibly Albania in the future, officials said.
